title: What Is a Wave?
hook: A wave moves energy from place to place without moving the stuff it travels through — the water bobs, but the wave races on.
key_points: A wave is a disturbance that transfers energy without transferring matter.
Transverse waves wiggle across the direction of travel; longitudinal waves squeeze along it.
Key traits: wavelength, frequency, amplitude, and speed.
Wave speed equals frequency times wavelength.
content_html: A wave is a traveling disturbance that carries energy through a medium without carrying the medium itself. Picture a cork floating on a pond: when ripples pass, the cork bobs up and down but doesn't drift across the water. The water stays put; only the energy moves.
extra_html: Waves come in two basic geometries. In a transverse wave the medium wiggles at right angles to the direction the wave travels, like a shaken rope. In a longitudinal wave the medium compresses and stretches along the direction of travel, like a pushed spring. Every wave is described by a few numbers: its wavelength (length of one cycle), frequency (cycles per second), amplitude (size of the disturbance), and speed — and those connect through speed = frequency times wavelength. Britannica surveys the types of waves and the quantities that characterize them.

related.title: Sound Waves
related.hook: Sound is just air being squeezed and stretched — which is also why there's no sound in the vacuum of space.

flashcards.prompt: What does a wave transfer, and what does it leave behind?
flashcards.back_html: A wave transfers energy from place to place but does not carry the matter along with it — the medium just oscillates in place.

flashcards.prompt: How do transverse and longitudinal waves differ?

choices.text: Transverse wiggle across the direction of travel; longitudinal squeeze along it
Transverse carry matter; longitudinal carry only energy
They are identical except for their speed

flashcards.explanation_html: The distinction is the direction of the disturbance relative to travel: across for transverse, along for longitudinal.

flashcards.prompt: Which relationship gives a wave's speed?
flashcards.explanation_html: Multiplying how often it cycles (frequency) by the length of each cycle (wavelength) gives how fast the wave travels.
